case_title: M. Nageshwar Rao v. State of Andhra Pradesh
accused_occupation: Faculty member at a computer institute (also gave coaching to students at another computer centre)
accused_socioeconomic_status: Earned a salary of about Rs.20,000 per month (only income detail stated)
accused_victim_relationship: Spouse (husband and wife); the judgment also describes marital frictions alleged in the confessional statement
weapon: Cyanide poison administered in a Limca cold drink bottle
evidence_type: Medical (post-mortem and forensic reports); oral evidence of witnesses (landlady, maid, shopkeeper); recovery of Limca bottle; disowned confessional statement (excluded)
confession: Detailed confessional statement attributed to the accused before police and panch witnesses; repudiated by accused, not supported by panch witness PW12; not relied on and excluded from consideration by the Supreme Court
trial_court_outcome: Acquitted of s.302 IPC; prosecution failed to prove guilt beyond reasonable doubt
high_court_outcome: State appeal allowed; acquittal reversed; convicted under s.302 IPC, rigorous imprisonment for life and fine of Rs.1,000 (default 3 months simple imprisonment)
neutral_facts: The victim, the accused's wife, was found unconscious in a chair in the rented first-floor flan the couple shared in a house owned by a landlady, and was taken to hospital by the landlady and her maid. The accused, who worked as a computer faculty member, arrived at the hospital later. The victim was declared dead the following day after repeated cardiac arrests. The post-mortem found cyanosis, froth in the mouth and nostrils, and a yellowish liquid in the stomach that smelled of bitter almonds. Forensic analysis of the stomach and organ samples found cyanide. The prosecution's case was that the accused bought a cold drink bottle from a general store, mixed cyanide into it at the house, and gave it to the victim, who had asked for a cold drink. The shopkeeper testified about the sale, but said he did not remember the buyer well and did not know where the buyer lived. A goldsmith said to have sold cyanide to the accused was examined, but he testified that police had coerced him into making his statement. A statement attributed to the accused before police, witnessed by two panch witnesses, was repudiated; one panch witness did not support it. An empty Limca bottle was later recovered from a shelf in the couple's bedroom and was found to contain cyanide, but the bottle reached the laboratory weeks after its recovery.
physical_harm: Death of the victim from cyanide poisoning
premeditation_planning: Not found by the court. Planning (buying cyanide, waiting for a chance) appears only in the disowned confessional statement, which the court excluded.
motive: alleged: marital frictions, the victim's refusal to cooperate and insistence on going to the U.S.A. with the accused (from the disowned confessional statement); not accepted by the court
key_evidence_accepted: Medical and forensic evidence that the victim died of cyanide poisoning; the testimony of the landlady and maid that the victim was found unconscious (not disputed). The court did not accept proof that the accused gave the cyanide.
witness_credibility: PW6 (shopkeeper) found unreliable; PW4 (goldsmith) retracted under police coercion, a major blow to the prosecution; PW12 (panch) hostile and denied recovery; PW18 (investigating officer) uncorroborated on the confession and bottle recovery; PW7 and PW3 gave accounts of finding the victim unconscious
post_offence_conduct: Alleged in the disowned confessional statement (feigned ignorance, discarded remaining liquid, concealed the bottle, tried to flee). Not accepted by the court.
custody_duration: Not stated (accused alleged custody from 4 September 2000 and formal arrest on 7 September 2000; the court did not decide this)
trial_duration: offence: September 2, 2000 (victim found unconscious; death September 3, 2000); trial judgment: not given; High Court: September 13, 2007; Supreme Court: January 5, 2011
legal_representation: Accused (appellant): Sushil Kumar, S. Udaya Kumar Sagar, Vinita Sasidharan, Aditya Kumar (Lawyer's Knit & Co.). State (respondent): D. Mahesh Babu, Ramesh Allan, D. Bharathi Reddy.
investigation_status: FIR registered; charge sheet filed; trial held and completed in the trial court
procedural_irregularity: Post-mortem samples reached the laboratory after 11 days without explanation; the Limca bottle reached the laboratory about 20 days after recovery without explanation; the seizure panch denied the recovery
appeal_history: Trial court: acquitted under s.302. High Court: State appeal allowed, acquittal reversed, convicted under s.302 with life imprisonment. Supreme Court: appeal allowed, conviction set aside, accused acquitted.
legal_principle_applied: Suspicion, however strong, cannot take the place of proof; a repudiated confessional statement not supported by other evidence is of no use and must be excluded from consideration
other_sentence_order: Accused to be released from jail forthwith unless required in another criminal case; High Court judgment set aside and trial court judgment restored
